MONTREAL YMCA 


Mission of the Montreal YMCA 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership of volunteers and 
staff committed to the fulfillment of people in spirit, mind 
and body and to the development of self-reliance in the 
individual and the community. 


Through its actions, programs and services, the Montreal 
YMCA reflects the needs and aspirations of communities 
and works with individuals, local communities and 
communities in developing countries in achieving social 
justice and control of their environments.”

MONTREAL YMCA 


Fiscal 2001-2002 was a pivotal year for the YMCA, because it marked 
the turning point between a rich historical past and a future full of 
promise. 


The Montreal YMCA’ 
come and how closely intertwined our history is with that of Montreal, 
its life and people. The celebrations were concrete proof of 
Montrealers’ attachment to “their Y”, which was further reinforced by 
people in top political and financial circles who clearly recognize the 
key social and community role of our institution. Numerous events — a 
commemorative stamp, local shows, a successful revitalization 


s 150" anniversary showed us how far we had 


campaign — culminated in a gala evening in November, which brought 
staff, volunteers and friends of the YMCA together. 


The retrospective gave us a great sense of pride in our 
accomplishments, and encouraged us to continue moving forward and 
thinking about our future. Our thoughts are summarized in a 
document titled Vision 2005. 


Our vision for the coming years is the result of an extensive 
consultation with our volunteers, staff and partners on their 
perceptions and expectations of the YMCA. The process showed that 
our action is based on a solid foundation with values that remain 
current, the drive to find innovative solutions, and a financial situation 
that will enable us to revitalize our facilities. 


We intend to make the most of our strengths to consolidate the 
organization in terms of our human, material and financial resources. 
We are looking to increase the reach of our programs and services — 
particularly through expansion — to benefit the largest number of 
people possible. Lastly, we would like to enhance the image of the 
Montreal YMCA with the general public and the media, so the solutions 
we propose to address current social issues help improve the quality of 
life of all Montrealers. 


I would like to thank Michael Weil, one of the architects behind the 
major rethinking process, who until recently was President & CEO of 
the Montreal YMCA. He had a tremendous positive impact on us while 
here in Montreal. We will, however, still have the pleasure of benefiting 
indirectly from his dynamic approach and generous spirit, since he is 
now the Chief Executive Officer of YMCA Canada. 


In closing, I wish to thank all our volunteers and staff from the bottom 
of my heart. The enthusiasm they displayed throughout the Vision 
2005 rethinking process will ensure a solid future for us. 


Sera At and 


Suzanne Aboud 
Chair of the Board of Directors 


BRUIS | '8; 


LEGUMES. 


DOWNTOWN YMCA - Spring Cleanup Rally 


On April 21, 2002, the Downtown YMCA held its 7° Annual Earth Day Cleanup Rally downtown in cooperation 
with the City of Montreal, Destination Centre-ville, Peter McGill Eco-Quartier and Earth Day. Over 
100 enthusiastic volunteers, including youth, adults and newly arrived refugees gave downtown sidewalks a good 
spring cleaning in the quadrant from Guy to Bleury and René-Lévesque to de Maisonneuve. 


McGill College Street was closed to traffic between Ste-Catherine and de Maisonneuve for the occasion to make 
way for a major environmental fair. Information kiosks, including Eco Fair, promoted healthy environmental 
practices. The Raging Grannies were on hand to talk about peace and the environment with their usual irreverent 
humour. Singers, dancers, and other performers also attracted hundreds of people to the site. 


In addition to encouraging Montrealers to take care of their environment, the event helped the Downtown YMCA 
raise $16,000 for its youth and refugee programs, as well as its partner YMCA in Ecuador. 


It was a wonderful day, made possible in part with the support of several sponsors, including Toyota Canada, 
Home Depot, Tourisme Montréal, the Eaton Centre, Oxford Quebec and Destination Centre-ville. 


DU PARE YMCA - My Very Own Neighbourhood 


Nathalie Rochefort, MNA for Mercier, invited youth at the Du Pare YMCA, L'Imagerie youth centre and Maison 
des jeunes on Plateau Mont-Royal to enter in a photo contest of their neighbourhood. 


What a great way to reinforce their sense of belonging, while discovering just how talented they can be! The youth 
went through every step of the process from choice of subjects. picture-taking, development and framing to 
organizing the actual exhibition. Participants from the Du Pare YMCA benefited from the support of a volunteer 
professional photographer throughout the process, which lasted six months. 


In addition to being proud of seeing their work on display, the youth gained a lot of experience. Some learned 
patience and concentration, or acquired new confidence in their ability to be successful and creative, while others 
found reason to continue with their studies. The young girl who won First Prize People’s Choice Award and 
Second Prize — Jury Award had never picked up a camera before... 


GUY-FAVREAU YMCA - Putting Children First... 


Always at the heart of the action, the Guy-Favreau YMCA is first and foremost driven by its will to meet the needs 
of children. 


In early 2001, El Salvador was hard hit by violent earthquakes that completely devastated entire villages. In 
partnership with the El Salvador YMCA, the centre undertook to set up a toy-lending library for some 
600 children in the temporary refugee camp in Santa Tecla. The centre collected new and used toys that will be 
shipped by container this fall. It hopes to bring a little happiness into the lives of children who have lost 
everything. 


Pol HUE COMMUNITY ) 


Here at home, the centre decided to offer new running shoes to every student at the Champlain primary school, 
located in the Centre-South district of Montreal — one of the city’s most underprivileged neighbourhoods. The 
collection was in the form of a twinning that matched every donor with a child. The donor was given a paper 
Easter egg with one child’s name, grade and shoe size. Centre volunteers were then able to give each child in the 
school a gift bag containing new shoes, along with other little surprises. Needless to say, the presentations were 


very touching. 


HOCHELAGA-MAISONNEUVE YMCA - 
Music to Get Teens on the Move 


Vincent Potel, the well-known Quebee backup singer, lost his brother, age 46, to a heart attack. Vincent is 
convinced that his brother would not have died at such a young age if he had taken the time to exercise and eat 
a healthy diet. which are habits we acquire as teenagers. 


Instead of lecturing youth about physical activity to no avail, Vincent decided that the best approach was to give 
them access to the right facilities and stimulating programs. All proceeds from the CD will go to the Montreal 
YMCA to benefit youth and low-income families. 


The CD, titled Le grand cour des choristes, is a true labour of love by Quebec singers and songwriters. Vincent 
produced fourteen songs, which were all specially composed for the occasion by local songwriters and musicians. 
The songs are performed by eighteen solo artists and some sixty background vocalists. 


To date, more than 700 CDs have been sold. That should give plenty of rhythm to the program! 


NOTRE-DAME-DE-GRACE YMCA - A Story to Tell 


For the past three years, the NDG YMCA Youth Department has celebrated Black History Month in a variety of 
ways. Once again this year, activities gave the community an opportunity to discover the richness of black culture. 


Staff and volunteers organized four introductory-level cooking nights featuring the traditional dishes of Nigeria, 
Trinidad, Jamaica and St. Vincent. Youth members even produced a small cookbook that was handed out to each 
participant, 


The NDG YMCA and Montreal Museum of Fine Arts, in cooperation with the Black Community Resource Centre, 
Black Women on the Rise, The Walkley Centre. Westhaven Centre and Lasalle Boys and Girls Club, hosted a 
family day on February 16 that attracted approximately 1,000 people. Activities at the highly successful event 
including an art exhibition, food tasting, hair braiding, films and face painting. 


On February 22, some 200 people attended a variety show at the YMCA that included song, poetry and dance 
performed by local talent. The evening. which began with an inspirational sermon by Rev. Darryl Gray, ended 
with a buffet, courtesy of local Caribbean restaurants, including Ma’s Place and La Bonne Bouffe, as well as Ben 
& Jerry's. The show was also sponsored by Ruby International, Echo Unlimited, Creative Solutions, The Trevor 
Williams All Star Basketball Academy and Lithium Clothing. 


POINTE-ST-CHARLES YMCA - Thanks for Calling! 


“T live alone, so being called every day makes me feel me safer. The “Thought for the Day’ that I hear when I pick 
up the phone gives me the encouragement | need to get the day off to a good start.” 


This woman is one of many P.A.I.R. subscribers, an individual assistance program for retirees. Comments like 
hers are what motivate volunteers to look for ways to improve the service they provide the community’s elderly. 


Since the daily call service was launched, a number of community groups and partners have joined forces with 
the YMCA, including the Pointe-St-Charles Community Clinic, the local police station, a locksmith, as well as the 
CLSCs in Southwest Montreal. We are working together to improve the program and reach as many people who 
live alone as possible. We must emphasize that (ate ing for this program was provided by the Mare ‘elle and Jean 


Coutu Foundation. 


ST-LAURENT YMCA - “Please Tame Me” 


Seniors from the Entre-Amis group and child volunteers in the St-Laurent YMCA Programme d’alimentation en 
milieux défavorisés (a program that delivers hot meals to underprivileged children) jointly staged The Little 
Prince by Saint-Exupéry as part of the Friendship Has No Age Intergenerational Week. The production was made 
possible through an OVEP (Organisme volontaire d’éducation populaire) grant and the support of the Fondation 
Sirois. 
Children and adults alike gained a lot from the experience, as you can see from the actors’ comments below: 

g i } 
“I learned that you have to take care of those you love, the same way I took care of my rose.” 
“We learned that you shouldn't be fooled by appearances. You have to see with your heart — not just your eyes.” 


“I discovered that theatre is fun, and The Little Prince taught me about the meaning of friendship.” 


“Forming relationships with different generations is really worth it. Big people should try to be closer to us, so we 
can learn how to trust them.” 


That pretty much says it all. 


WEST ISLAND YMCA 
Fitness Personality Profile Generates Interest and Activity 


The new Fitness Personality Profile orientation program has generated a lot of activity at the centre. The program, 
developed by Jim Gavin who has a Ph.D. in Psychology, is very much in keeping with the YMCA’s mission to 
promote overall personal development of the spirit, mind and body. 


Using a computerized questionnaire, the Fitness Personality Profile enables members to discover the benefits 
(other than physical) of their training or select the types of training that are best suited to their personality, which 
in turn increases their motivation and perseverance. 


At the West Island YMCA, some 1,500 members have already completed the questionnaire, and approximately 
150 of them have attended orientation workshops. To date, 35 volunteers and staff members have taken Fitness 
Personality Profile counsellor training. To respond to growing demand, we plan to offer the course to one hundred 
or so employees and volunteers by year end. 


WESTMOUNT YMCA - Getting to Know Our Neighbours 


The centre started the year with a local, national and international partnership project that will take our youth 
all the way to Nicaragua. 


The first step brought teens together from the Westmount and Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCAs. As they became 
better acquainted at Kamp Kanawana, in the two centres and during weekend exchanges between families, the 
youth learned about economics, international development and studied Spanish together. A number of them 
discovered a another part of Montreal they knew nothing about. 


Once the Montreal group established a connection, they all ventured off to be hosted by the rural community of 
Cobourg, Ontario. Several weeks later, youth from Cobourg visited their new friends in Montreal. Together they 
began raising funds for their trip to Central America. 


By working together in this way, the youth developed strong ties that went beyond all social, cultural, economic 


and linguistic differences. They found that you don’t have to go to the end of the world to be open to others, 
learned tolerance in the face of diversity and the spirit of cooperation. 


YMCA KAMP KANAWANA - A Year of Firsts 


In 2001-2002, Kamp Kanawana experienced a record-breaking year and a number of firsts as well. 


During the summer, the camp welcomed more than 220 campers, up 19% from last year. Registration has never 
been this high! 


In November, a large number of the summer campers met up again at the Westmount YMCA for Kamp Kabaret 
— an evening of songs, skits and laughs. 


For the first time ever, Kamp Kanawana launched a winter camp for children and youth between the ages of 
7 and 16. Campers enjoyed four days of cross-country skiing, snowshoeing and sledding, along with the requisite 
hot chocolate and grilled marshmallows around the fireplace at the end of the day. 


Kanapalooza was another first for the camp that could well become an annual event. Monitors past and present 
staged a benefit concert at Club Soda and raised $2,000 for Kamp Kanawana. 


INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMS - 
Inauguration of the YMCA of Haiti 


The new YMCA in Port-au-Prince began its activities with the opening of the Konbit Youth Centre. The Creole 
name sets the tone for the centre, since the word “Konbit” means the pooling of community resources to carry out 


important work. 


In 1996, the Latin American Confederation of YMCAs approached the Montreal YMCA for help, which has 
supported the project ever since. Establishing a YMCA in an impoverished country is not easy. The focus was 
therefore placed on Haiti’s youth, who represent the future of the country. International Programs staff and 
representatives from various Montreal YMCAs, including Frédéric Boisrond, Director of the 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve centre, travelled to Haiti to plan the project, in addition to training local staff and 
volunteers. Others, like the du Pare YMCA, contributed from afar with a shipment to Haiti of some 400 books 
and magazines to help set up a library. 

In the short time since it opened, the Youth Centre already has a membership of 500 children and youth, who are 
attracted by the wide range of programs available. such as a reading club, sports clubs, language courses, dance 


classes, discussion groups, leadership training, ete. 


The values promoted by the new centre are proudly painted on the wall to remind youth of what unifies YMCAs 


the world over: respect, honesty, responsibility and self-reliance. 


To0th ANNIVERSARY OF THE MONTREAL YMCA 


On November 24, some 600 employees, volunteers and guests danced with heart, soul (and body!) to celebrate 
150 years of community action by the Montreal YMCA. 


7001-2002 MONTREAL YMCA SOCIAL RESULTS 


In 2001-2002, the Montreal YMCA facilitated access to its programs and services for more 
than 3,458 people who were in financial difficulty. 


Also, through its programs and activities, the Montreal YMCA reached 126,244 people in 


2001-2002.

FOUNDATION INC. 


THE MONTR 


Message from the chairman of the board of directors and 
President of the Montreal YMCA Foundation 


The role of the Foundation is to ensure long-term funding 
for the Montreal YMCA so all of our centres can play a 
front-line role in the community, while providing access 
for all to our programs. 


This year, the Foundation took part in the Jision 2005 
process — a major rethinking of the direction the YMCA 
is taking. In light of this new direction and fortified by a 
successful revitalization campaign, which helped raise 
over $3.5 million, the Foundation set new challenges for 
itself to secure the organization’s long-term independence 
and viability. 


The Foundation intends to use a variety of means to 
support all types of community action in YMCAs and the 
expansion of the Association as well, such as a greater 
number of partnerships, more diversified sources of 
funding, a growing endowment fund (currently 
$3.5 million), higher annual campaign objectives, etc. 


In fact, work is already well under way. This year, the 
Foundation’s board of directors recruited new members 
for its next major fund-raising campaign. In addition, the 
funds raised by the annual golf tournament to benefit the 
YMCA’s youth programs increased 17 percent. 


We wish to thank the members of our Board, as well as all 
volunteers and staff of the Foundation for their ongoing 
effort and exceptional commitment. The YMCA*s 
community action is by and large dependent on their 
efficiency and dedication. 


ae (eee 


Claude A. Garcia Marcel Coté 
Chairman of the Board President of the Montreal 
YMCA Foundation

Annual golf tournament 
ee 


The 17" annual Montreal YMCA Golf Tournament, which drew 153 people to the Pinegrove Golf and Country 
Club on Monday, June 3, 2002, helped raise $52,121. The funds were used to finance several Montreal YMCA 
youth programs. 


We wish to thank the 26 sponsors of our event. 


Special thanks to our Patrons of Honour: , 
BMO Nesbitt Burns k 
Fasken Martineau DuMoulin 

Hervé Pomerleau Ine. 

Imperial Tobacco Canada Ltd. 
Langlois Gaudreau, S.E.N.C. 
National Bank of Canada 

RBC Capital Markets 

Samson Bélair Deloitte & Touche 
Sermax Inc. 

St. Lawrence Cement Inc. 
Standard Life 


We also wish to thank the numerous individuals and companies that donated door prizes and gifts for the silent 
auction. 


Our heartfelt thanks to the volunteers who helped make the tournament a great success: 
Bryan McMahon, G. André Petit and Jacques Luys.
